description: OpenTerrace provides a Python framework for simulating packed-bed thermal energy storage. Its contributors publish modular thermal models that can be extended with material representations and used within system studies or optimisation loops. The software is independent of a named geographic area. Users choose the geometry, numerical nodes, time step and simulation duration, not receiving a fixed observation period or resolution. The first documentation tutorial configures a one-dimensional cylindrical water domain, prescribed boundary temperatures and mass flow, then plots temperature profiles. Source code is on GitHub, and the README links installation and usage documentation. GitHub identifies GPL-3.0 as the code licence, allowing free use under its conditions. Limitations include the need to choose numerical schemes and material assumptions appropriate to the storage design; review of documentation alone does not establish accuracy for a proposed installation. The model supports assessment and sizing of thermal storage. Related record model-energyplus covers whole-building energy simulation; this is a thematic relationship, not a verified coupling. The tutorial was read without running it.
